2026-10-22 asr-quality T-ASRQ-04: canonical transcript segments carry confidence = exp(min(0, avg_logprob)) x (1 - no_speech_prob) of their raw segments, a 0-1 review hint rounded to three decimals. A projected segment keeps its raw value weighted by its owned (clipped) duration; cross-window duplicates and fully trimmed boundary fragments fold into the kept cue as a duration-weighted mean, and an overlap repair reweights the moved cue by its adjusted span. Timing, text, merge, shaping, retry and quality decisions are unchanged; the field is optional in the transcript schema, so older transcripts stay valid. The legacy-parity replay strips only this reviewed field. 2026-10-23 asr-quality T-ASRQ-11: after the cross-window merge the post-processor reports window seam duplicates in report.seamDuplicates (cue ids, times, seam, clipped edge, coverage and kept cue ids; no text): a cue whose raw observation straddled an overlapping core seam and was clipped to it, when it has at least 2 CJK or 4 Latin comparison characters (NFKC, lowercase, without punctuation and whitespace) and the fewest insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn them into one contiguous stretch of the cues across the seam whose raw observations overlap its own (joined in time order) are at most 20% of them, reported as coverage = (characters - edits) / characters; the next window's clipped cue is judged first and a dropped cue is never compared again. A cue that already keeps an earlier reported duplicate is reported only when that duplicate still reaches 80% with its remaining kept cues, and that entry then lists only those, so a kept cue is never reported across consecutive seams. The canonical transcript and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision are unchanged; the exported dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates removes a reported cue only while it and its kept cues keep their reported timing and wording (separators aside) and none of its kept cues is removed with it. 2026-10-24 asr-quality T-ASRQ-11 review: the seam comparison is local (closest contiguous stretch) instead of a whole-text in-order common subsequence, so a short reply whose characters only occur apart in a longer cue across the seam is no longer reported; every earlier T-ASRQ-11 case keeps its decision and coverage. 2026-10-24 asr-quality T-ASRQ-11 refinement after the real-audio rerun: (1) far-end guard: a clipped cue is not reported when at least 2 CJK or 4 Latin of its comparison characters at its far end (away from the seam: the end of a next-window cue, the start of a previous-window cue) have no counterpart in the closest stretch across the seam, counting only the trailing characters that no fewest-edit alignment pairs with any character across the seam, matched or substituted (so only characters past the end of the other side's text count, and far-end characters that merely differ still count toward the coverage), so a copy the other window stops short of keeps its words; the previous window's clipped fragment that the kept copy fully covers is then judged and reported in the previous-window pass. Edits elsewhere still count toward the 80% coverage, and judging an earlier decision again applies the same guard. (2) Edge restore: an entry may carry restoredEdge {cueId, edge, fromMs, toMs} (no text) naming its kept cue that is clipped to the same seam on the opposite edge (start of a next-window kept cue, end of a previous-window kept cue); toMs is its raw edge, never past the reported cue's far edge, capped by maxCueDurationMs against the other edge (an end against the start already restored at the cue's earlier seam, since seams are judged in time order) and omitted when no move remains; an entry whose restored cue a later decision reports loses it. dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates moves that edge only together with the drop (all kept cues unchanged), never over the nearest remaining cue on that side, never changes text, and returns each dropped entry with the edge it actually restored or without restoredEdge. The canonical transcript and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision are unchanged. 2026-10-24 asr-quality T-ASRQ-14 (AC-ASRQ-14-6): a clipped cue the far-end guard keeps is remembered with its seam (seamDuplicateCoverage now returns "far_end" for the guard instead of undefined; every drop, coverage and restore decision is unchanged). The entry at that seam whose kept cues include it (the other window's clipped copy dropped in its favour) may carry trimmedEdge {cueId, edge, removedChars, fromMs, toMs} (no text) when the kept copy's seam-side comparison characters (the start of a next-window copy, the end of a previous-window copy; NFKC, lowercase, without punctuation and whitespace) are exactly all those of the nearest canonical cue on that side that no entry reports, the text breaks there at punctuation or whitespace (removed with the repeated words; removedChars counts the removed graphemes), and at least 2 CJK or 4 Latin comparison characters remain. fromMs is that edge as the reported restores leave it; toMs is the neighbour's end (start), capped by maxCueDurationMs against the other edge as restored, and never inward. dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates applies it after the entry's restore and only together with the drop, while that reported neighbour (the next cue once every reported duplicate is gone) is still beside the kept copy, has its reported timing and wording and was not moved in the same call; it rechecks the wording on the current text, moves the edge only outward, never over the neighbour nor past the planned bound, and returns the entry with what it removed and where the edge moved, or without trimmedEdge. This is the only case in which a kept cue's text changes. The canonical transcript and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision are unchanged. 2026-10-24 asr-quality T-ASRQ-14 review: (1) a lone apostrophe, hyphen, dot or middle dot between letters or digits (don't, e-mail, 3.5) sits inside a word and is no break, so the report plans no trimmedEdge there and dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates keeps such a copy whole; (2) when one kept copy is trimmed at both its seams, the later planned trim is capped by maxCueDurationMs against the earlier trim's planned bound instead of the other edge as restored, so the trimmed copy stays within the longest cue. Every drop, coverage, restore and other trim decision is unchanged, as are the canonical transcript and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision. 2026-10-24 asr-quality T-ASRQ-16: new export retimeLocalSubtitleSegmentsFromAnchor (with the LocalSubtitleAnchorRetiming and LocalSubtitleAnchorRetimingStatus diagnostics types; LocalSubtitleAnchorRetiming.status also names the executor outcomes failed, rejected and skipped) moves a preset window's raw segments (window-relative ms) onto the times of the same audio recognized with the standard request fields. Both texts are compared as across seams (NFKC, lowercase, without punctuation and whitespace) and paired character by character along one longest common subsequence; a window above 1e6 character pairs is not compared ("oversized"). A segment's start takes an anchor segment's start when its first two characters pair with that anchor segment's first two adjacent characters, and its end takes an anchor segment's end when its last two pair with that segment's last two; every other edge moves by the shift linearly interpolated along the preset times between the nearest anchored edges before and after it in segment order, or by the nearest one's shift beyond the outermost (rounded to ms). Starts then stay at or after the previous end and every segment lasts at least 200 ms within [0, window duration]; where the window end leaves a segment short, it and those before it move earlier, but no edge that took an anchor time does, and a window where one would have to keeps its segments. A window without an anchored edge or such a fit ("unaligned"), without anchor text ("empty"), with an invalid duration or with text the contract would refuse keeps its segments unchanged. Text and every other segment field are unchanged; the result reports anchored and total edges and the median and largest edge shift (no text). Only the Studio executor calls it, for audio-profile tasks; postProcessLocalSubtitleTranscript, dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision are unchanged, so the default-path replays are unaffected. 2026-10-25 asr-quality T-ASRQ-16 follow-up (design option 9, retime only windows heard early): after alignment retimeLocalSubtitleSegmentsFromAnchor retimes a window only when the median of its anchored edges' signed shifts (anchor minus preset time, later is positive; the lower middle of an even count, so more than half of them) is at least LOCAL_SUBTITLE_ANCHOR_RETIMING_MIN_MEDIAN_SHIFT_MS (500 ms, exported next to the other retiming constants); otherwise it returns the preset segments unchanged with the new status "not_early", its anchored and total edge counts, that median and the largest anchored edge shift either way. medianShiftMs is now that anchored-edge median for retimed windows as well (it was the lower median of every edge's final shift, interpolated and fitted edges included); maxShiftMs of a retimed window is unchanged. Alignment, interpolation, the order and length fit, the unaligned, oversized and empty outcomes, text and every other segment field are unchanged. postProcessLocalSubtitleTranscript, dropLocalSubtitleSeamDuplicates and every merge, shaping, retry and quality decision are unchanged, so the default-path replays are unaffected.

Anchor requests spend no requestsPerRoot budget (so separator and seam repairs keep their eligibility), are never retained, are assessed only to accept them, and never feed text, confidence or post-processing; a window whose preset segments have no text sends none. An accepted anchor's segments retime that window's attempt through retimeLocalSubtitleSegmentsFromAnchor (from the already imported post-processor module; no new import). The retimed attempt is assessed again with assessLocalSubtitleRawWindow and decideLocalSubtitleWindowRetry under the task policy, as postProcessLocalSubtitleTranscript assesses every attempt, and replaces the window's attempt before post-processing only when still accepted, so merge, seam duplicates and the optional CUDA repairs read the retimed segments and retiming never makes post-processing refuse a window; otherwise the window keeps its times (status rejected). A failed, rejected, mismatched or empty anchor keeps the window's times and the task continues; cancellation and cleanup failures propagate as before. Progress: an audio-profile task reports totalWindows = 2 x root windows and advances completedWindows through the anchors within the transcribing stage (30 to 80 percent), never backwards. transcript_ready.anchorRetiming returns per-window diagnostics (windowIndex, startMs, endMs, anchorSegments, anchoredEdges, totalEdges, medianShiftMs, maxShiftMs, status; no text), which the document never receives. Tasks without an audio profile send exactly the same requests, report the same progress and return exactly the same result as before. 2026-10-25 asr-quality T-ASRQ-16 follow-up: comment only.
